name: Sam Sample
headline: Lead Frontend Engineer
summary: Frontend engineer with twelve years of experience building web applications for travel, publishing and public-sector clients. Works mostly in Vue and TypeScript, with a strong interest in internationalisation, forms and search. Prefers small, steady releases, plain documentation and close work with support teams, and is at ease owning a feature from the first sketch to the support queue.

bullets: Rebuilt holiday search on Elasticsearch facets, so results load in under a second for 90% of queries.
Added right-to-left layouts and eleven new locales to the booking site, with translators working in a shared glossary.
Wrote the error-budget policy the frontend team uses to choose between new work and fixes.
Joined the weekly support rotation and turned the top ten ticket causes into backlog items.
Built the newsroom's article editor with live previews for print and web layouts.
Cut image weight on article pages by serving responsive sizes from a resizing service.
Moved paywall rules from templates into a tested rules module shared by web and apps.
Delivered council application forms that work without JavaScript and save progress between visits.
Ran usability sessions with residents and fed the findings into the form design guide.
Set up automated accessibility checks in the release pipeline.
Maintained the shop's product pages and seasonal landing pages.
Wrote the stock-sync script that kept the website in line with the warehouse system.
Kept the library website and events calendar up to date and ran drop-in computer sessions.

projects: Open-source Vue plugin for pluralisation rules in twenty languages, used by several travel sites.
Small static site generator for walking-route guides, with offline maps and printable pages.
